primitives.name: Play-Level Charting Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: **"Hand-graded every play of the season"** — a labor claim.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\epsilon_{\\text{chart}}': 'error rate in automated play tagging (dimensionless)', '\\eta': 'human correction factor (unitless scaling)'}
primitives.assumptions: Human review reduces \epsilon_{\text{chart}}; the correction is additive and bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \epsilon_{\text{chart}} > threshold, indicating systemic automation failure requiring manual override.

layer2.mapping: GSE maps automated charting errors to a correction kernel \eta \cdot \Delta_{\text{chart}}, where \Delta_{\text{chart}} is the discrepancy between automated and corrected tags.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of charting errors corrected manually per play type

primitives.name: Ranking vs. Actuals
primitives.verbatim_quote: theirs, same players, same weeks, same metric, published before kickoff, scored after.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_i': 'rank of player i in the ranking system', 'A_i': 'actual performance score of player i', 'D(R, A)': "discrepancy measure between rank and actual (e.g., Kendall's tau)"}
primitives.assumptions: Rankings are ordered by expected performance; discrepancies arise from model bias or noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D(R, A) exceeds statistical significance, indicating ranking instability or misalignment.

layer2.mapping: GSI evaluates ranking quality via D(R, A) using empirical datasets, enabling iterative refinement of the projection core.
layer2.telemetry: Kendall's tau correlation between predicted and actual player rankings

The core operators are defined by the interplay between automated projection pipelines and human-in-the-loop corrections. The Projection Accuracy Gap (Δ_proj) measures how well a model predicts outcomes, while the Play-Level Charting Correction (ε_chart) quantifies the benefit of human review in reducing systematic tagging errors. These two metrics define a dual space: one where model performance is evaluated, and another where human oversight adds variance reduction. The Ranking vs. Actuals (D(R,A)) operator bridges these spaces by comparing predictions to outcomes, establishing a feedback loop for both systems. Failure modes include model drift (when Δ_proj increases), automation collapse (when ε_chart exceeds acceptable bounds), and ranking instability (when D(R,A) grows beyond tolerance). The system is robust if these operators remain within defined regimes, with GSI providing probabilistic guarantees and GSE ensuring dynamic adaptation.
